  "hook": "Xinomavro translates directly to \"acid-black,\" a name that perfectly previews the aggressive structure of this Northern Greek grape. Sourced from the limestone and clay soils of the Giannakochori estate on Mount Vermio, Ramnista tames that natural ferocity through careful oak aging. It serves as the benchmark for modern Naoussa, bridging traditional savory notes with polished fruit.",
  "wine_summary": "Yiannis Boutaris left his massive family wine empire in 1997 to focus on site-specific expressions at Kir Yianni. Today, under his son Stellios, the estate defines what contemporary Naoussa tastes like. By mapping the different soil blocks of their Mount Vermio vineyards, they isolated the parcels that give Xinomavro its best chance at full phenolic ripeness\u2014crucial for a grape notorious for harsh, green tannins if picked too early or planted in the wrong exposition.\n\nNaoussa PDO strictures demand 100% Xinomavro, and Ramnista delivers the textbook profile: a medium garnet color belying massive structural grip. The continental climate of Macedonia, marked by cold winters and cooling mountain winds during the summer, preserves the grape's trademark high acidity while allowing the signature aromas of sun-dried tomato and olive tapenade to develop fully. Multiple gold medals at the TEXSOM International Wine Awards confirm its consistency across vintages.",
  "terroir_expression": "Mount Vermio's eastern slopes provide the elevation and sun exposure necessary to ripen Xinomavro's thick skins. The Ramnista blocks sit on a mix of calcareous clay and sandy loam. The clay retains moisture during dry Macedonian summers, keeping the vines functioning to develop dark cherry flavors, while the active limestone drives the wine's piercing acidity and chalky mineral finish. Cold mountain air flowing down the slopes at night slows ripening, which builds the grape's complex savory aromatic profile\u2014think dried herbs and tomato leaf\u2014without spiking the alcohol.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fermentation takes place in stainless steel tanks with a pre-fermentation cold soak\u2014a technique where crushed grapes are chilled to delay yeast activity, extracting color and fruit aromatics before alcohol develops and pulls out bitter seed tannins. Following fermentation, the wine ages for roughly 16 months in a mix of French and American oak casks and barriques. This extended wood aging is non-negotiable for Ramnista; the porous oak allows slow oxygen exposure (micro-oxygenation) that softens Xinomavro's fierce, jagged tannins into a more approachable texture while integrating notes of baking spice.",
  "food_pairing": [
    "Smoked brisket with a vinegar-based BBQ sauce\u2014The wine's high acidity cuts through the heavy rendered fat, while its savory tomato-leaf notes echo the tang of the sauce.",
    "Mushroom risotto with aged Parmigiano-Reggiano\u2014Xinomavro's earthy, underbrush aromas lock in perfectly with the umami of the mushrooms, and the cheese's salt softens the wine's aggressive tannins.",
    "Lamb gyros with extra tzatziki\u2014A casual weekday pairing where the high-toned acidity acts like a squeeze of lemon over the heavy, spiced meat, cleansing the palate between bites.",
    "Braised short ribs with root vegetables\u2014The slow-cooked protein binds with the wine's firm tannic structure, making the wine feel richer and fruitier than it does on its own."
  ],
  "comparable_wines": [
    "Produttori del Barbaresco Langhe Nebbiolo \u2014 Shares the exact same structural profile of pale-to-medium color, high acid, and high tannin, plus similar aromatic notes of dried red fruit and earth.",
    "Domaine Katsaros Valos Xinomavro \u2014 Another benchmark Northern Greek Xinomavro, though typically slightly lighter in body and more floral than the muscular Ramnista.",
    "Lopez de Heredia Vi\u00f1a Tondonia Reserva \u2014 Offers a similarly savory, high-acid, extended-aged profile with notes of dried cherry and old leather, appealing to the same palate."
  ],
  "style_profile": "100% Xinomavro delivering medium-bodied weight, aggressive tannins, and distinct savory aromas of sun-dried tomato",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Keep this in a cool, dark cellar for at least five years past the vintage date to let the tannins relax. It will comfortably evolve for 15 to 20 years, shifting from tart red fruit to complex leather and tobacco.",
  "value_assessment": "At $29.46, this represents an absolute steal for a structure-driven, age-worthy red wine. You would easily pay $45 to $60 for an entry-level Barolo from Vietti or Massolino that delivers this exact level of complexity and tannic grip. It punches far above its weight class and deserves to be bought by the case.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers at Mediterranean-focused restaurants use Ramnista as their secret weapon for guests who ask for big Italian reds but want to try something new. It rarely dominates retail end-caps, instead living in the Greek wine section waiting for adventurous buyers and hardcore wine geeks who understand its aging potential. You will not find casual sweet-wine drinkers reaching for this due to its fiercely dry, savory nature.",

parsed.hook: Xinomavro translates directly to "acid-black," a name that perfectly previews the aggressive structure of this Northern Greek grape. Sourced from the limestone and clay soils of the Giannakochori estate on Mount Vermio, Ramnista tames that natural ferocity through careful oak aging. It serves as the benchmark for modern Naoussa, bridging traditional savory notes with polished fruit.
parsed.wine_summary:
Yiannis Boutaris left his massive family wine empire in 1997 to focus on site-specific expressions at Kir Yianni. Today, under his son Stellios, the estate defines what contemporary Naoussa tastes like. By mapping the different soil blocks of their Mount Vermio vineyards, they isolated the parcels that give Xinomavro its best chance at full phenolic ripeness—crucial for a grape notorious for harsh, green tannins if picked too early or planted in the wrong exposition.

Naoussa PDO strictures demand 100% Xinomavro, and Ramnista delivers the textbook profile: a medium garnet color belying massive structural grip. The continental climate of Macedonia, marked by cold winters and cooling mountain winds during the summer, preserves the grape's trademark high acidity while allowing the signature aromas of sun-dried tomato and olive tapenade to develop fully. Multiple gold medals at the TEXSOM International Wine Awards confirm its consistency across vintages.
parsed.terroir_expression: Mount Vermio's eastern slopes provide the elevation and sun exposure necessary to ripen Xinomavro's thick skins. The Ramnista blocks sit on a mix of calcareous clay and sandy loam. The clay retains moisture during dry Macedonian summers, keeping the vines functioning to develop dark cherry flavors, while the active limestone drives the wine's piercing acidity and chalky mineral finish. Cold mountain air flowing down the slopes at night slows ripening, which builds the grape's complex savory aromatic profile—think dried herbs and tomato leaf—without spiking the alcohol.
parsed.vinification_summary: Fermentation takes place in stainless steel tanks with a pre-fermentation cold soak—a technique where crushed grapes are chilled to delay yeast activity, extracting color and fruit aromatics before alcohol develops and pulls out bitter seed tannins. Following fermentation, the wine ages for roughly 16 months in a mix of French and American oak casks and barriques. This extended wood aging is non-negotiable for Ramnista; the porous oak allows slow oxygen exposure (micro-oxygenation) that softens Xinomavro's fierce, jagged tannins into a more approachable texture while integrating notes of baking spice.
food_pairing: Smoked brisket with a vinegar-based BBQ sauce—The wine's high acidity cuts through the heavy rendered fat, while its savory tomato-leaf notes echo the tang of the sauce.
Mushroom risotto with aged Parmigiano-Reggiano—Xinomavro's earthy, underbrush aromas lock in perfectly with the umami of the mushrooms, and the cheese's salt softens the wine's aggressive tannins.
Lamb gyros with extra tzatziki—A casual weekday pairing where the high-toned acidity acts like a squeeze of lemon over the heavy, spiced meat, cleansing the palate between bites.
Braised short ribs with root vegetables—The slow-cooked protein binds with the wine's firm tannic structure, making the wine feel richer and fruitier than it does on its own.
comparable_wines: Produttori del Barbaresco Langhe Nebbiolo — Shares the exact same structural profile of pale-to-medium color, high acid, and high tannin, plus similar aromatic notes of dried red fruit and earth.
Domaine Katsaros Valos Xinomavro — Another benchmark Northern Greek Xinomavro, though typically slightly lighter in body and more floral than the muscular Ramnista.
Lopez de Heredia Viña Tondonia Reserva — Offers a similarly savory, high-acid, extended-aged profile with notes of dried cherry and old leather, appealing to the same palate.
parsed.style_profile: 100% Xinomavro delivering medium-bodied weight, aggressive tannins, and distinct savory aromas of sun-dried tomato
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Keep this in a cool, dark cellar for at least five years past the vintage date to let the tannins relax. It will comfortably evolve for 15 to 20 years, shifting from tart red fruit to complex leather and tobacco.
parsed.value_assessment: At $29.46, this represents an absolute steal for a structure-driven, age-worthy red wine. You would easily pay $45 to $60 for an entry-level Barolo from Vietti or Massolino that delivers this exact level of complexity and tannic grip. It punches far above its weight class and deserves to be bought by the case.
parsed.market_position: Sommeliers at Mediterranean-focused restaurants use Ramnista as their secret weapon for guests who ask for big Italian reds but want to try something new. It rarely dominates retail end-caps, instead living in the Greek wine section waiting for adventurous buyers and hardcore wine geeks who understand its aging potential. You will not find casual sweet-wine drinkers reaching for this due to its fiercely dry, savory nature.
parsed.insider_take: Opening a current-vintage Ramnista is a tactical error unless you plan to decant it for four hours. The sheer density of the tannins will strip the moisture from your gums and hide the fruit entirely if drunk too young. Buy it, hide it in the back of your closet for a decade, and you will have a wine that drinks like aged Barbaresco for a fraction of the cost.
